4bb0ee06ca.text:
DFV takes its name from the most famous act of conviction in retail investing
          history — holding when every incentive said sell. It is a meme coin, and it is
          not shy about that. What it refuses to be is the other kind of meme coin: the
          one with a hidden team wallet, an unannounced unlock, and a founder quietly
          exiting into his own community.

b120e7c9b2.text:
So the tokenomics were built the other way round. There is no team allocation.
          There is no private round waiting to dump. There is no mint function, so the
          supply that exists is the supply that will always exist. 84.51% of every DFV
          token was placed into a public Uniswap pool at launch, where anyone can see it
          and anyone can trade against it.

a5b7f52480.text:
The 15% that isn't liquid belongs to the Blind Believers — the people who backed
          this before there was anything to back. It is locked in a vesting contract for
          five years, with nothing at all released in year one. Governance runs on-chain
          through a DAO with a timelock, so no decision takes effect the moment it passes.

c899427033.text: We are driven by the following 10 commandments that define the whole business model.

6edee0fe58.text: Thou Shalt Have No Other Memes Before DFV

7339f1b34b.text: DFV shall do everything to become the GREATEST OF ALL MEMES, ensuring it is the only meme worthy of worship in the crypto world.

6e712006df.text: Thou Shalt Uphold Integrity Above All

a04da09c9a.text: DFV shall maintain the highest ethical standards, holding transparency, fairness, and community-driven decisions as core principles.

d6c4477299.text: The community's well-being is paramount, and all mechanisms, including penalties, are designed to prevent exploitation and ensure fair treatment.

978993376f.text: All purchase prices shall be official and transparent, eliminating hidden or manipulated valuations.

6986be8294.text: No investor shall dump tokens on the community. A sky-high burn penalty will be applied to any investor sale without community approval.

68ae140e33.text: Thou Shalt Ask the Community for the Final Commandments

0e1bddb982.text: DFV shall honor its community by seeking their wisdom to craft the remaining commandments, ensuring that the project is shaped by the very people it serves.

b7caebfbb9.text: DFV shall celebrate and reward its most loyal supporters. Those who hold steadfast will receive benefits that grow with their commitment to the project.

6ea5a1b856.text: DFV shall constantly evolve, seeking new ideas, innovations, and strategies to stay ahead in the meme coin landscape. Stagnation is not an option.

96a302b625.text: DFV shall empower its community with knowledge, providing resources to help every member make informed decisions.

944e507516.text: Thou Shalt Spread Joy and Humor Above All

22ca2294d3.text: DFV is here to make the crypto world more fun. With every post, meme, and community interaction, DFV shall spread joy, laughter, and positivity.

d8073de4f9.text: The vesting contract has a public read function, <0>getClaimableAmount</0>. You can call it on Etherscan with your address and see exactly what's available — no wallet connection, no signature, no risk.

582d8da6f9.text: Nothing unlocks in the first year. Zero percent is released at the start, and after the one-year cliff your allocation begins releasing continuously — second by second — across five years.

bd5964d075.text: When you have a balance available, <0>claim()</0> sends it to your wallet. Tokens are never pushed to you automatically; they wait in the contract until you ask for them.

c1ffed4faf.text: How DFV governance works: delegate your vote, propose, and decide. Deliberately slow, deliberately expensive.

d2ba6c56b6.text:
DFV is governed by whoever holds and delegates DFV. Everything on this page is read
    straight from the contracts — the interface can do exactly what the code allows, and
    nothing else.

5fc2946864.text:
Holding DFV gives you <0>no voting power at all</0> until you delegate it —
      including to yourself. This catches nearly everyone. One transaction, once, and your
      balance starts counting.

5df9360173.text: Read live from <0>0xFa85F00e72B4EfD4d02BB252CdAE23EeE8294508</0>. These are not our description of the rules — they are the rules.

4ce1229b2a.text:
14 days before voting opens, then 30 days to vote —
        44 days minimum from proposal to decision. Long
        enough that nobody is rushed, and far too long for a borrowed-token governance attack to survive.

27072e686d.text:
Filing a proposal needs 694,200,000 DFV delegated — roughly $159,969 at
        the current market price. Proposals therefore cost real conviction, and spam is priced out entirely.

43b2e6b02c.text:
Voting power is not handed out. It is bought on the open market and delegated. Every vote
        represents someone who paid for their say at the same price as everyone else.

1e112acd8f.text:
Most DFV cannot vote. 117,495,846,526 sits in the Uniswap pool and 20,821,732,113 is
      locked in the vesting contract — neither delegates, so neither has a voice. Voting power only
      exists once tokens are held in a wallet <0>and</0> delegated.

cf73633d6b.text: In the Uniswap pool — cannot vote

1a45e255a1.text: 2.51% of the tokens needed for quorum currently exist in a form that could vote.

d3f8a9c0d8.text:
<0>Governance is not active yet.</0> Quorum needs 20,826,000,000 DFV of delegated
      votes, and at most 522,421,361 could vote today even if every holder delegated.
      That gap closes as DFV is bought out of the pool and as vested tokens are claimed and delegated —
      roughly $4,799,069 of tokens must move into voting hands before the DAO can decide anything.
      Until then this page is honest about it rather than pretending otherwise.

e8be68e660.text:
No proposals have been filed. The first requires 694,200,000 DFV delegated to a single
      address. When one exists it will appear here, with its live state, tallies and every vote reason
      recorded on-chain.

7df32fd66b.text:
491,353,345.96 DFV is held in a <0>2-of-6
      Gnosis Safe</0> at <1>0xaF786e8cDD7E4390BD629bfDec8f090268FE2934</1>.

c64e28d0df.text:
Being explicit, because it matters: the DAO contract cannot move these funds by itself. A vote
      decides, and the Safe signers execute. The multisig exists so the treasury cannot be lost to a
      single mistake or a single key — the trade-off is that spending it takes a human signature as well
      as a vote.

a11fab5bd5.text:
The token itself is immutable: six functions, no mint, no burn, no pause, no upgrade, no owner.
      The supply that exists is the supply that will always exist. Governance parameters live on the DAO
      contract and can only be changed by a passed proposal.

Every month, the address with the highest trading volume receives

2247f2ed89.text:
Every DFV transfer in or out of the Uniswap V4 PoolManager is collected, then
      each transaction is checked against the events the pool itself emitted. Only
      transactions containing a <0>Swap</0> event are counted as trades.

49e065a4f1.text:
<0>This is why the numbers are honest.</0> 5 transactions
      moved DFV in or out of the pool as <1>liquidity</1> rather than trading — including the
      initial provision of roughly 117.5 billion DFV. Counting those as "sales" would
      inflate volume by a factor of thousands. They are excluded, and listed separately
      in the raw JSON.

b8e8015175.text:
The trader shown is the account that signed the transaction, not the router
      contract that appears as the counterparty in the transfer — so aggregators and
      routers never appear on the leaderboard in place of real people.

13fa69caef.text: Ten thousand tickets, one hundred winners, drawn by Chainlink. No admin, no pause, no way to pick the winners. See the mainnet rehearsal.

05ab502f18.text:
Ten thousand tickets at 100 USDC. One hundred winners drawn by Chainlink — a Rolex and
    ninety-nine cash prizes of 4,000 USDC. When the last ticket sells, the draw happens on its
    own. Nobody can stop it, delay it, or choose who wins.

ea6baf7da4.text:
Chainlink is producing the randomness for this
        round. Entries reopen automatically with the next one.

50d01737cb.text:
Buying takes two transactions: approving the exact USDC these tickets cost, then the
        purchase itself. The approval is never unlimited, and this page can send no other
        transaction of any kind.

17694a3118.text:
The moment the last ticket sells, or six months after the first one, the draw
        triggers. Anyone can trigger it, and a keeper does it automatically — so it does not
        depend on us being awake, or willing.

6f305907f3.text:
Chainlink VRF produces the randomness with a proof that is checked on-chain before
        the contract can use it. We deliberately do not use block data, which a miner could
        re-roll.

fc918c7898.text:
No owner, no pause, no upgrade, no withdrawal function. The house address is fixed
        at deployment and no code path sends USDC anywhere else. Nothing can be changed
        afterwards — including by us.

cbbecb2543.text: You can always take your prize

1246a21e14.text:
Prizes are paid out in batches automatically, but if that ever stops, a winner can
        pull their own prize directly from the contract at any time. It does not expire.

0c673e1b99.text:
<0>40.8% of everything collected is paid back out as prizes</0> — the watch plus
      the ninety-nine cash prizes. The rest is the house's. That share is fixed in the contract
      and cannot be changed.

7329991faa.text:
This holds whether the round fills or not. A round that sells nine thousand tickets pays
      the same 40.8%, scaled down, so nobody gains from a round failing to fill. Below 500
      tickets the round is cancelled instead and buyers take back 80% of what they paid.

90ecd3a4b8.text:
A raffle is not an investment. Most tickets win
      nothing, and the expected return on a ticket is less than what you paid for it. Only buy
      what you are happy to lose.

71c60ea549.text: It has already been run, with real money

288df53006.text:
Before opening, we ran a complete round on Ethereum mainnet at one fifty-thousandth of
      the size — real USDC, real Chainlink randomness, our own money. Two thousand tickets,
      one hundred winners, every prize delivered, nothing left in the contract.

74c22d736d.text:
Before the raffle took a single real entry, we ran a complete round on Ethereum mainnet
    with our own money — real USDC, real Chainlink randomness, at one fifty-thousandth of the
    size. It worked. Every transaction below is on the public chain and you can open all of them.

c4d32b606f.text:
2,000 tickets sold, 100 winners drawn by Chainlink VRF, all 99 cash prizes delivered,
    and

2a414271c2.text:
The round collected 20.00 USDC and paid out 20.00 USDC. Because this was a rehearsal, the
      same address was the house <0>and</0> every winner, so all of it came back — but the
      contract did not know that, and split it exactly as it will in a real round.

bc405418bf.text:
Winners are drawn by <0>Chainlink VRF v2.5</0>, which produces a random number
      together with a cryptographic proof that it was not tampered with. The proof is verified
      on-chain before our contract is allowed to use it. Nobody — not us, not a miner, not
      Chainlink — can pick the winners.

4029518de9.text:
We deliberately do <0>not</0> use block data for this. A block proposer can see values
      like <1>prevrandao</1> before publishing, and could quietly re-roll a
      draw worth a million dollars. Chainlink costs more and is worth it.

679c69f027.text:
All 100 distinct, all inside the 0–1,999 range. The first drawn ticket
      (<0>1501</0>, in red) takes the watch; the other 99 take cash.

207fdec061.text:
In the order the contract delivered them. Ticket 1501 is absent because it won
      the watch, which is a physical object handed over off-chain rather than a transfer.

7e1cf0e58d.text: What this does and does not prove

7fe0a98552.text:
Real USDC moved, real randomness arrived, the arithmetic came out exact, and the
        contract emptied itself to the last cent without anyone intervening.

eba40decde.text: It does not replace an audit

7bb9d257a0.text:
A working rehearsal shows the contract does the right thing when nobody is attacking
        it. That is a different question from whether it resists someone with a million dollars
        to win, and only a professional audit answers the second.

d8b55c8114.text:
This rehearsal contract is <0>not</0> the one a real round will use. It is
      configured at one fifty-thousandth scale, and its house and guardian addresses are the
      test wallet. The production contract is deployed separately and its address will be
      published here and on the raffle page before it accepts a single ticket.
